deletion_policy.description:
Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the instance. Defaults to "DELETE".
When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the instance,
the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.
deletion_policy.rationale: Controls whether Terraform is prevented from destroying the document schema. Setting this to 'PREVENT' guards against accidental or unauthorised deletion via 'terraform destroy'/'apply' - the same destructive-loss-prevention pattern already enforced on google_compute_interconnect and google_compute_node_group's deletion_policy. Losing the schema breaks is_required/type validation for every document that depends on it, and the default 'DELETE' allows that with no safeguard.

display_name.description: Name of the schema given by the user.
display_name.rationale: A human-readable label with no bearing on access, exposure, or data handling.

document_is_folder.description: Tells whether the document is a folder or a typical document.
document_is_folder.rationale: Structural flag distinguishing a folder-type document from a regular one; it does not alter who can access it or how it is indexed.

location.rationale: Determines the region/zone where the resource is created. Policy should restrict it to an approved-region whitelist for data residency; the allowed set is parameterised (a hardcoded example whitelist is acceptable).

project_number.description: The unique identifier of the project.
project_number.rationale: A resource identifier/scoping value; project-level access is governed by IAM bindings elsewhere, not by this attribute.

property_definitions.description: Defines the metadata for a schema property.

property_definitions.display_name.description: The display-name for the property, used for front-end.
property_definitions.display_name.rationale: A front-end label for the property, no access or exposure implication.

property_definitions.is_filterable.description: Whether the property can be filtered. If this is a sub-property, all the parent properties must be marked filterable.
property_definitions.is_filterable.rationale: Controls whether the property's value can be used as a structured query filter - a retrieval/indexing behaviour, not an access-control boundary. Actual document access is governed by IAM/warehouse-level permissions elsewhere, not by per-field search/filter flags.

property_definitions.is_metadata.description: Whether the property is user supplied metadata.
property_definitions.is_metadata.rationale: An internal tagging flag for derived properties; interpretation is left to the API caller and has no access-control effect.

property_definitions.is_repeatable.description: Whether the property can have multiple values.
property_definitions.is_repeatable.rationale: Controls cardinality (single vs. multiple values), not visibility or access.

property_definitions.is_required.rationale: A data-completeness/validation rule (must the value be populated), not an access or exposure control.

property_definitions.is_searchable.description: Indicates that the property should be included in a global search.
property_definitions.is_searchable.rationale: Setting this true includes the property's value in the warehouse-wide global search index, making it discoverable via search by any principal with query access to the corpus. The risk is specific to properties holding sensitive/classified content - for a non-sensitive property, searchability is a functional choice with no security implication. It should default to false and only be enabled once a property has been confirmed non-sensitive.

property_definitions.name.description: The name of the metadata property.
property_definitions.name.rationale: The property's identifier; naming does not affect who can see its value.

property_definitions.retrieval_importanc.description: Stores the retrieval importance. Possible values: ["HIGHEST", "HIGHER", "HIGH", "MEDIUM", "LOW", "LOWEST"]
property_definitions.retrieval_importanc.rationale: Only weights ranking of a property among search results that are already returned; it does not gate whether the property is exposed via search (that is is_searchable).

property_definitions.date_time_type_opti.description: Date time property. Not supported by CMEK compliant deployment.

property_definitions.enum_type_options.p.rationale: The controlled vocabulary for an enum property - defines valid content, not who can see it.

property_definitions.enum_type_options.v.description: Make sure the enum property value provided in the document is in the possile value list during document creation. The validation check runs by default.
property_definitions.enum_type_options.v.rationale: A data-quality validation toggle (does the value have to match the enum list); it does not grant or widen access to the property's value.
